articles.content: Ports and Shipping 1 min read Built by private shipyard, Navy gets 1st indigenous MPV INS Samarthak, India's first multi-purpose vessel, was officially commissioned into the Indian Navy at Karwar naval base. The vessel will function as a mothership for various unmanned and autonomous vehicles, enabling advanced testing. TIMESOFINDIA.COM Updated On Oct 17, 2026 at 04:02 PM IST Select ETInfra as Preferred Choice on Google Copy Link Share on WhatsApp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook India’s first multi-purpose vessel (MPV), INS Samarthak. India's first multi-purpose vessel (MPV), INS Samarthak , built by a private shipyard , was commissioned into Indian Navy during a ceremony at Karwar naval base in Karnataka Friday, reports Surendra Singh. INS Samarthak will be the first-of-its-kind vessel that will act as a mothership for unmanned and autonomous surface and aerial vehicles, a testbed for weapons and sensors, a platform for maritime surveillance , towing, disaster relief and also double up as a hospital ship. Vice-President C P Radhakrishnan, along with Navy chief Admiral Krishna Swaminathan and Karnataka labour minister Santosh Lad, led the commissioning ceremony. Advt The vessel has more than 75 per cent indigenous content. articles.title: ISRO's AstroSat Uncovers Cosmic Mysteries, Delivers Breakthrough Insights Into the Universe
articles.content: India ISRO’s AstroSat Uncovers Cosmic Mysteries, Delivers Breakthrough Insights Into the Universe October 17, 2026 · 2 min read Facebook Twitter WhatsApp India’s space observatory AstroSat has made significant contributions to astronomy, helping scientists explore some of the universe’s most mysterious phenomena. Launched by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) on September 28, 2015, AstroSat is India’s first dedicated multi-wavelength space observatory.Unlike observatories that study celestial objects within a limited range of wavelengths, AstroSat can observe cosmic sources across ultraviolet, visible light and X-ray wavelengths. This capability allows scientists to examine different aspects of the same object and gain a deeper understanding of its behaviour. Major Discoveries in Space Over the years, AstroSat has helped scientists investigate black holes, neutron stars, distant galaxies and powerful stellar explosions. Its observations of the black hole system GRS 1915+105 have provided valuable information about rapid changes in X-ray emissions and the behaviour of matter surrounding black holes.Another notable achievement was the detection of extreme-ultraviolet light from a distant galaxy, AUDFs01, located approximately 9.3 billion light-years from Earth. The discovery demonstrated AstroSat’s ability to observe faint signals from the distant universe. These findings have strengthened India’s contribution to international astronomical research and provided scientists with new data to investigate the evolution and behaviour of celestial objects. How AstroSat Differs From NASA’s Observatories AstroSat offers a distinctive advantage through its ability to observe cosmic objects simultaneously across multiple wavelength ranges using instruments aboard a single satellite. This helps researchers compare observations taken at the same time.NASA operates several advanced space observatories, including the Chandra X-ray Observatory, which specialises in studying the universe through X-rays. AstroSat and Chandra have different capabilities and scientific strengths, making their observations valuable for complementary research. Rather than establishing that AstroSat is universally more accurate than NASA’s observatories, its achievements demonstrate India’s growing capabilities in space-based astronomy. A Major Milestone for Indian Space Science Initially designed for a minimum useful life of five years, AstroSat continued operating beyond its planned lifespan, completing 11 years in orbit in September 2026.Its continuing scientific contributions highlight the capabilities of Indian scientists and research institutions involved in developing and operating the mission.As researchers continue analysing its observations, AstroSat remains an important instrument for exploring black holes, distant galaxies and other unexplained phenomena, expanding humanity’s understanding of the universe. articles.title: Aster CMI Hospital Performs India's First Paediatric Kidney Transplant Through Donor Swap
articles.content: Medi News Facebook Twitter Linkedin Aster CMI Hospital, Bengaluru, reported a significant milestone in kidney transplantation by facilitating a two-way kidney donor swap between two families, enabling a 15-year-old boy and a 21-year-old man to receive life-saving kidney transplants. According to the hospital, this is India’s first reported paediatric kidney transplant involving a donor exchange to overcome blood group incompatibility. Both patients had family members willing to donate a kidney. However, blood group incompatibility prevented the donors from donating directly to their intended recipients. To overcome this challenge, the hospital facilitated a kidney-paired donation (KPD), allowing the two families to exchange donors so that each patient could receive a more suitable kidney. The procedure highlights how advanced donor-matching technology and coordinated transplant care can expand opportunities for patients who cannot undergo direct living-donor transplantation. Donor-Matching Technology Enables a Two-Way Kidney Swap Aster CMI Hospital used donor-matching software from the Alliance for Paired Donation (APD) to identify suitable donor-recipient combinations for the exchange. Through this approach, the teenager received a kidney from the donor associated with the 21-year-old patient’s family, while the adult patient received a kidney from the teenager’s family donor. This exchange enabled both patients to proceed with transplantation despite the incompatibility that had prevented direct donation. Kidney-paired donation is an established transplant strategy that connects incompatible donor-recipient pairs with other pairs whose donors may be better suited to their intended recipients. Depending on the circumstances, this approach can help address blood group or human leukocyte antigen (HLA) incompatibility. By evaluating donor-recipient pairs systematically, matching software can help transplant teams identify suitable exchanges and improve access to living-donor kidneys. However, every proposed match still requires detailed medical evaluation to establish compatibility and minimise risks. Also Read | Flower-derived compound inhibits enzyme linked to multiple sclerosis and cancer Months of Planning and Coordinated Surgical Care The two-family kidney swap required months of planning, detailed coordination and collaboration among multiple medical specialties. According to the hospital, the complex procedure involved four operating theatres functioning simultaneously, supported by four anaesthetists and four transplant surgical teams. Infectious disease specialists also contributed to the multidisciplinary effort. Such coordination is essential in paired-donation procedures because the participating transplant operations must be carefully synchronised. Furthermore, the medical teams must assess donor suitability, recipient compatibility and patient safety at every stage. The successful completion of the procedures demonstrates the role of coordinated surgical planning and specialised transplant infrastructure in managing complex living-donor kidney transplantation. Doctors Highlight the Benefits of Kidney-Paired Donation Dr. Arun Kumar N, Senior Consultant – Nephrology and Renal Transplant, Aster CMI Hospital, said, “It is time India shifts from the conventional transplant method to ABO-incompatible kidney transplants to ensure the best possible outcomes from the first attempt. This is a precision and target-driven transplant assuring 99% adaptability. This gives a better perspective on survival, longer graft survival and does away with repeated transplants. articles.title: China Drafts Export Controls on Solar, AI and Biotech Technologies - GKToday
articles.content: Home China Drafts Export Controls on Solar, AI and Biotech Technologies China Drafts Export Controls on Solar, AI and Biotech Technologies October 17, 2026 Current Affairs Today - Latest Current Affairs - 2026-2027 China’s Ministry of Commerce and Ministry of Science and Technology jointly published a draft revision to the Catalogue of Technologies Prohibited and Restricted from Export on 16 October 2026. Titled “Announcement No. 48”, it proposes a complete export ban on 14 technologies and export restrictions on 26 others across artificial intelligence (AI), photovoltaics and biomedicine. Export controls and technology transfer Export controls regulate the transfer of specified goods, software or technical knowledge beyond a country’s borders. China’s draft plan proposes pre-export registration for the listed technologies; the interim registration requirement took effect on 16 October 2026 and also applies to unfinished deals. A public consultation on the draft runs until 15 November 2026. China’s Ministry of Commerce cited national security, prevention of technology misuse and inappropriate proliferation, and the need to keep AI under human control as reasons for the proposed controls. Technologies already publicly available through open-source publication or academic papers are generally exempt under the proposal. Photovoltaic manufacturing chain The draft lists 12 photovoltaic technologies covering polysilicon production, wafer manufacturing and solar-cell manufacturing. Listed technologies include perovskite and tandem solar-cell module manufacturing. Restrictions also cover polysilicon engineering technologies used in production lines with annual capacity of at least 30,000 tonnes. The proposal concerns selected technologies; other photovoltaic technologies would remain freely exportable. Artificial intelligence and biomedicine The draft covers 23 AI-related technologies, including foundation models, intelligent agents, computing clusters and information-processing technologies. It proposes a complete export ban on AI-driven technology capable of generating and mutating malicious code. The proposal also lists five biomedical technologies, including cell and gene therapy platforms, small nucleic-acid drugs and pathogen-related technologies. Important Facts for Exams The draft proposes 14 complete export bans and restrictions on 26 other technologies. The photovoltaic technology list covers polysilicon, wafers and solar-cell manufacturing. The AI list includes foundation models, intelligent agents and computing clusters. The public comment period ends on 15 November 2026. Open-source publications and academic papers that place technologies in the public domain are generally exempt from the proposed export controls. articles.title: Aditya-L1 Gives ISRO A Solar Edge - Rediff.com
articles.content: 'It is to observe the Sun continuously that you have the Aditya L1 mission.' 'It is in a position from where it can observe the Sun continuously.' It was in 2023 that ISRO launched its highly ambitious space mission, Aditya L1, India's first dedicated space-based solar observatory designed to study the Sun. Unlike the earlier NASA and ESA sun missions, Aditya L1 is positioned at the Sun-Earth Lagrange Point 1 (L1) to have an uninterrupted view of the sun without the eclipses or occultation. With plenty of data to study, Aditya L1 is considered as a very successful space mission. Professor R Ramesh is Senior Professor at the Indian Institute of Astrophysics and Principal Investigator for the Visible Emission Line Coronagraph (VELC) payload on the Aditya-L1 mission. "The biggest advantage of having an observatory, a spacecraft, observing the Sun in the Lagrange L1 point is, unlike what we see on the Earth where we have this day-night cycle, the Sun rising in the morning and setting in the evening, in the Lagrange L1 point, you continuously see the Sun," Professor Ramesh tells Rediff 's Shobha Warrier . How important was the Aditya L1 mission, and how exciting was the data from the mission for scientists? As far as the Aditya L1 mission is concerned, as the word L1 in the title indicates, it is about the Lagrange L1 Point. L1 is the direct line between the Sun and Earth, about 1.5 million kilometres away from the Earth toward the Sun. The biggest advantage of having an observatory, a spacecraft, observing the Sun in the Lagrange L1 point is, unlike what we see on the Earth where we have this day-night cycle, the Sun rising in the morning and setting in the evening, in the Lagrange L1 point, you continuously see the Sun. In short, there is no day-night cycle there. Because of its positioning? Yes, that is correct. It's because of the exact positioning that you are able to observe the Sun 24 hours a day, all the 7 days a week, and all the 365 days in a year. This type of continuous observation is very important in the study of the Sun because there are a large number of the eruptive phenomena that take place in the Sun's atmosphere, which we call as the Coronal Mass Ejections ( CME s). The mass of Coronal Mass Ejections can be 10 to the power of 15 grams. And it can travel at the maximum speed of 3,000 kilometres per second all the way up towards earth. Of course, there can be CMEs with lower speeds also. Typically, it carries an energy of approximately 10 raised to the power of 30 Ergs. Though the Coronal Mass Ejections can take place anywhere on the surface of the Sun, near the centre of the Sun and also on the edge of the Sun. articles.title: ISRO completes critical separation tests for Gaganyaan mission - DT Next
articles.content: CHENNAI: ISRO has successfully completed a series of Crew Module-Service Module (CM-SM) separation tests, marking a crucial step towards ensuring astronaut safety in India's first human spaceflight mission, Gaganyaan, the space agency announced on Friday. The Gaganyaan mission aims to send a three-member crew to a low Earth orbit (LEO) at an altitude of about 400 km for three to seven days before bringing them safely back to Earth, with a sea splashdown in Indian waters. According to ISRO, the Gaganyaan Orbital Module comprises the crew module (CM), which houses the astronauts, and the service module (SM), which supports the crew module during the mission. The two modules are connected through a separation system, while electrical and fluid services are maintained through umbilical connections. The modules remain integrated from launch until the completion of the orbital phase. Before the spacecraft re-enters Earth's atmosphere, the crew module must separate from the service module through a series of precisely sequenced operations involving pyrotechnic devices and jettisoning systems. To validate the overall design and reliability of the separation system, ISRO established a test setup at the Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (VSSC) in Thiruvananthapuram. The setup simulated the integrated CM-SM assembly and was equipped with extensive instrumentation to assess the separation process, including the severing of multiple umbilical connections between the modules. The tests also demonstrated the robustness and shock survivability of several critical crew module subsystems, including avionics systems, inertial navigation systems, the thermal protection system in the aft and conical heat shields, and the deployable umbilical shield. In addition, the tests assessed the ability of pyrotechnic devices associated with the Crew Module Uprighting System and the Thermal and Humidity Control System to withstand the separation sequence. The successful completion of the tests provides confidence in the performance of the CM-SM separation system ahead of the first uncrewed Gaganyaan mission, which ISRO is targeting for launch by the end of 2026.

articles.title: Kakinada to Launch India's First Electric Fishing Boat - Urban Acres
articles.content: Home Breaking News Kakinada Set to Launch India’s First EV Fishing Boat Breaking News Kakinada Set to Launch India’s First EV Fishing Boat By Urban Acres October 17, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Kakinada is set to host the experimental launch of an electric fishing vessel, marking the reported beginning of Suraas Ventures Limited’s planned pan-India marine electric-vehicle operations. The launch, described by the company as the first of its kind in India, is scheduled to take place in Kakinada with MLA Vanamadi Venkateswara Rao, also known as Kondababu, expected to inaugurate the boat. The electric fishing vessel is being manufactured by Suraas Ventures Limited as part of an effort to reduce fishing boats’ dependence on diesel. The company says the project is intended to lower fuel costs for fishermen, reduce environmental impacts and introduce electric propulsion and other clean technologies into the fisheries sector. According to V.V. Rao, the company’s technical director and a retired additional director of the fisheries department, the boat can operate for six hours on a durable battery. He said this duration would be sufficient for local fishermen who venture out daily. The report does not provide details on the battery’s capacity, charging infrastructure, vessel speed, carrying capacity or the cost of the electric boat. The Kakinada launch is being positioned as an experimental step rather than a full-scale commercial rollout. The company has said it plans to expand its operations across India and internationally over the next 24 months. Its stated target groups include fishing committees, tourism operators, government institutions and commercial marine stakeholders. The proposed expansion places Kakinada at the centre of a wider industrial ambition. Suraas Ventures Limited says the city could develop into a manufacturing and service hub for marine electric vehicles, supporting production, maintenance and other services for electric boats. Any such expansion would depend on the performance of the initial vessel, the availability of charging and maintenance systems, and the ability of operators to adopt the technology. These details have not been established in the supplied report. For fishing communities, fuel expenditure is a direct operating cost, making propulsion technology relevant to the economics of daily trips. However, the practical usefulness of an electric vessel will also depend on how long it can operate under actual fishing conditions, how quickly it can recharge and whether charging facilities are accessible near landing centres. The company’s six-hour operating claim is based on its statement and has not been independently evaluated in the supplied material. The initiative also raises an infrastructure question for coastal cities: electric marine transport cannot scale through vessel manufacturing alone. It requires suitable shore-side power systems, charging points, technical support, battery-handling arrangements and operating protocols. The report does not state whether these facilities are already available at Kakinada or whether they are part of the company’s planned expansion. V.V. Rao said the company may pursue a memorandum of understanding with the state and central governments if the first electric marine boat succeeds. The proposed MoU,...

articles.title: Ladakh's Development Momentum - Daily Excelsior
articles.content: When Prime Minister Narendra Modi virtually inaugurated five projects worth around Rs 3,350 crore in Ladakh on Thursday, the occasion was more than ceremonial. It marked another step in a sustained effort to bring one of India's most remote and demanding territories into the mainstream of development. For a region with a small population but an unforgiving terrain, the scale of the commitment is striking. The projects themselves speak to the breadth of the Government's thinking. A new passenger terminal at Kushok Bakula Rimpochee Airport in Leh, built for Rs 640 crore, is described as India's first to use geothermal heating. The 298-km Nimmu-Padum-Darcha Road, built by the Border Roads Organisation, strengthens both strategic and civilian connectivity. A 9 MW small hydroelectric project at Hanu and a 66 kV Dah-Hanu-Khaltsi transmission line address power needs, while 40 water bodies across 40 villages under Project Him Sarovar tackle water scarcity. India's first Petroglyph Conservation Park at Sindhu Ghat adds heritage protection to the list. Few packages manage to combine infrastructure, energy, water and culture so coherently. The process did not begin on Thursday. The first major decision was to carve out Ladakh as a Union Territory, giving it an administrative identity and the prospect of self-sustained growth. What followed was a steady build-up of institutions and infrastructure: universities, colleges, hospitals, roads and digital connectivity. Sceptics once wondered whether a region of such sparse population could justify investment on this scale. The Government has answered that citizens in difficult geography deserve the same opportunities as anyone else, and that strategic frontier areas cannot be left behind. Connectivity remains the defining challenge. Ladakh's isolation has long been dictated by the seasons, with high passes closing for months and cutting off communities. Special attention is now being paid to all-weather links from both the Srinagar and Manali sides. Tunnels are being sanctioned, built and inaugurated, and within the next few years the dream of year-round road access should become a reality. Alongside it, the plan for multiple airports and helipads would make even remote pockets reachable in extreme weather. For residents, this means access to medical care in emergencies, steadier supply chains and fewer months of enforced isolation. For tourism, it promises a longer and more reliable season. What distinguishes the Ladakh agenda is its attention to the environment. The region is ecologically fragile, and the Government has rightly sought to match development with restraint. Geothermal heating in the new terminal, solar power and small hydroelectric projects form part of a deliberate shift towards clean energy. Such first-of-their-kind initiatives show that modern infrastructure and environmental care need not be opposing. Ladakh's youth have long faced a difficult choice between staying home with limited prospects and migrating to distant cities for education and work. The proposed centre of excellence in Leh, together with satellite campuses of IIT Jammu and IIM Jammu, aims to change that equation by offering advanced research and technical skills at their doorstep.
